> woodwardlg.com is being blocked by AdGuard DNS Default (resolves to sinkhole 94.140.14.33). The Non-filtering server 94.140.14.140 returns the correct IP 159.65.34.143, confirming this is a blocklist entry rather than a resolution issue.

I don't have Oppo devices. If you are not using AdGuard filtering DNS (default/family) - just inblock these domains in DNS user filter, and using AdGuard Assistain - unblock for this app only.

- for DNS User Rules
- 
```
@@||cl-data.ads.heytapmobi.com^
@@||adsfs.heytapimage.com^
```

- for regular User Rules (add package_name to `$app`)

```
@@||cl-data.ads.heytapmobi.com^$app=
@@||adsfs.heytapimage.com^$app=
```

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.hulu.com/watch/a7976d43-3985-4dc2-9099-ec1767d6a031](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.hulu.com%2Fwatch%2Fa7976d43-3985-4dc2-9099-ec1767d6a031) ### Comment > It used to be that using Adguard on Hulu let you fast forward through commercials and the captions and pic would get out of sync, and you'd have to click "watch credits" in order to see the end of the episode because things would be, by the end of a show, 4-5 minutes out of sync. Now with Adguard running you can still ffwd through commercials, but the "out of sync" problem makes it so the episode will end early, sometimes just cutting off a few minutes sometimes cutting off over 5 minutes (whatever is after the last commercial). ### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://play.hbomax.com/video/watch-sport/7b2a25cc-b973-540f-aa45-1ee93d6644df/6bacd0aa-71c6-4626-a9a4-64c72b09ee2d](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fplay.hbomax.com%2Fvideo%2Fwatch-sport%2F7b2a25cc-b973-540f-aa45-1ee93d6644df%2F6bacd0aa-71c6-4626-a9a4-64c72b09ee2d) ### Comment > The following rule breaks rewinding on live streams: > > ``` > play.discoveryplus.com,play.hbomax.com#%#//scriptlet('xml-prune', 'xpath(//*[name()="MPD"]/@mediaPresentationDuration | //*[name()="Period"]/@start | //*[name()="Period"][not(.//*[name()="SegmentTimeline"] or .//*[name()="ContentProtection"])] | //*[name()="Period"][./*[name()="BaseURL"]][not(.//*[name()="ContentProtection"])])', '', '.mpd') > ``` > > Unlike VODs, live streams start with a `<Period start=` that is not 0, so stripping that breaks the scrub bar. > > Live streams don't really have "inserted" ads (they have natural ads as a part of the TV channel's live broadcast output), so might be worth checking for `MPD@type`: https://dashif.org/Guidelines-TimingModel/#timing-and-presentation-types (live streams have `dynamic` while VODs have `static`) ### Screenshots

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.hulu.com/watch/a7976d43-3985-4dc2-9099-ec1767d6a031](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.hulu.com%2Fwatch%2Fa7976d43-3985-4dc2-9099-ec1767d6a031) ### Comment > It used to be that using Adguard on Hulu let you fast forward through commercials and the captions and pic would get out of sync, and you'd have to click "watch credits" in order to see the end of the episode because things would be, by the end of a show, 4-5 minutes out of sync. Now with Adguard running you can still ffwd through commercials, but the "out of sync" problem makes it so the episode will end early, sometimes just cutting off a few minutes sometimes cutting off over 5 minutes (whatever is after the last commercial). It's inconsistent how much time is lost but with AdGuard running there's no way to see the last few minutes of the episode, you have to turn it off, let it reload, watch a few commercials, in order to see the last few minutes of each episode. Sorry I might not have answered a lot of the questions correctly or given you screen shots that are useful -- the questions you ask in order to submit an issue are so extremely technical (overly technical, frankly, to report a problem with a service I pay for). ### Screenshots

comment.body:
HTTPS exclusions are a little different than filter lists where it requires each supported AdGuard application to release an update as it's built within the app. They explain it on the repo readme here: https://github.com/AdguardTeam/HttpsExclusions#how-the-list-gets-updated-in-the-adguard-apps

Based on what I read there, what I would do for now is either:
1. manually add `westpac.com.au` to the HTTPS exclusions like you did previously, and when a new update of AdGuard for Windows is released, reset the HTTPS exclusions list back to default (if possible, otherwise resetting all settings), and update the app, so you have the list back to being dynamically updated; or
2. quit AdGuard entirely from the system tray when you need to use the Westpac live chat widget, and relaunch it when you're done.

It's not exactly the most convenient thing, and I wonder if they should incorporate a similar method like filter updates into their products for HTTPS exclusions. My guess is that these types of updates are not as common, so they haven't done so. As to why the exclusions list no longer gets updated when manually modified, is probably also due to the inability to merge changes made, and is safer than replacing the list forcefully and losing user-made changes.

I might send feedback in that repo actually about what I just said, as it does make these types of situations inconvenient.
